class: A check and the action it is meant to gate (push, merge, deploy) issued as separate parallel tool calls: the action does not wait for the check, so a failing check gates nothing; a same-command chain guard (gate_before_commit) cannot see across calls.
mechanism: The orchestrator sent `python scripts/ruff_ratchet.py` and `git commit && git push` as two tool calls in one message. They ran concurrently; the push landed while the ratchet printed 'ruff ratchet: FAIL, 1 rule(s) rose: C901'. The project hook gate_before_commit blocks `check; push` and `check | ... && push` inside ONE command, so it never saw the two calls.

first_seen.where: GC-2b item 1, W-091 (commit 7da1c24 pushed to PR #343)
first_seen.evidence: ratchet output 'FAIL, 1 rule(s) rose: C901' in the same message whose other call pushed 7da1c24; CI app-tests run 38961942455 then refused it ('ruff ratchet: C901 rose 80 -> 81')

fix: Habit: a gate and its action are never parallel calls - either one command `gate && action`, or the gate's result is read before the action is sent. Structural option (open): a push wrapper that runs the local gates itself (like land.py runs the close check) so the push cannot happen without them.

detection.note: CI caught it after the push; the cost was one red CI round.

occurrences.evidence: 7da1c24 pushed with C901 risen; fixed in 1daacc4
